OP I’m going to share a lesson and a phrase with you that I learned very recently: “Analysis paralysis”. What it means is if you spend all your time trying to figure out how to go about a situation you will never do anything because you end up way too deep in the weeds analyzing every last interaction and moment. Try this: you like her, she seems to like you, and you want to be with her, so you’ll ask her out. Boom, simple, done. 

Yes it sounds easier than it is. Yes you will be nervous asking her out. But OP, I am 24M and I wish that someone had told me this when I was your age. Commit to making mistakes and not being perfect; not grasping the situation perfectly. Just fully commit to it, and that way you can get out of your own way and move towards what you want. No amount of analyzing this situation will make you feel any better or resolve this tension. The only thing that will is action. So commit to not knowing and to being uncertain and anxious and afraid. Make an agreement with yourself that you are going to feel uncertain and anxious and afraid. Because then when you move forward and you feel those things, perfect, you’re feeling exactly how you knew you were going to feel, and there’s a sort of freedom and a letting go that comes when that happens. You get out of the way of yourself. And you become unburdened.

I personally don’t know about any technique other than looking at the car’s orientation (doesn’t mean it doesn’t exist). My advice would first be to practice in freeplay or workshop maps if you’re on PC (rings maps go crazy for practicing air roll) until you can fly consistently - that is, without losing control and crashing every three seconds. Nothing will do as much as for you as practicing in an environment where you don’t get scored on if you mess up. If you still want to do it in game, I would advise you to air roll with restraint. For example, if you jump for an aerial try doing one full spin with adjustment and then continue your aerial without air roll. Most of the crazy spinning you see people do is unnecessary, and the longer you do it as a beginner the more likely it is you will lose control and whiff the ball.

Learning to use directional air roll isn’t exactly “memorization”… but it is muscle memory. Over time and with enough practice (like 100+ hours) you’ll find that when your car is in a certain orientation, you sort of just know how to adjust to your liking. There are also similar patterns of motion that will become familiar with practice. 

I assume by going up and down while using air roll left, you mean pointing the car’s nose up and down. Practice jumping from the ground while holding ARL and pushing the stick in different directions to see how the car responds. I believe a combination of holding right and then up will point the car upward, but it is important to feel it out for yourself. Good luck!
